title: SCSS: Securing a ₹20,500 Monthly Income for Senior Citizens
description: The Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) is a government-backed scheme designed to provide a stable income for Indian senior citizens. It offers predictable.

faq.q: Who is eligible to invest in the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS)?
faq.a: Indian citizens aged 60 years or above are eligible. Individuals between 55 and 60 years who have retired on superannuation or VRS can also invest within one month of receiving retirement benefits.

faq.q: What is the maximum amount I can invest in SCSS?
faq.a: The maximum investment limit for an individual in SCSS is ₹30 lakhs across all accounts. The minimum investment is ₹1,000, and investments must be in multiples of ₹1,000.

faq.q: How often is the interest paid out from an SCSS account?
faq.a: Interest from SCSS accounts is paid quarterly. The payouts typically occur on the first working day of April, July, October, and January.

faq.q: Are SCSS investments eligible for any tax benefits?
faq.a: Yes, investments made in SCSS qualify for a deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961, up to a limit of ₹1.5 lakh per financial year.

faq.q: Can I withdraw my money from SCSS before the five-year maturity period?
faq.a: Premature withdrawals are allowed, but they come with penalties. A 1.5% deduction applies if withdrawn after one year but before two years, and a 1% deduction applies if withdrawn after two years but before five years.

faq.q: What happens to the SCSS account after the initial five-year tenure?
faq.a: Upon maturity, the investor has the option to extend the account for an additional three years. This extension must be done within one year of the maturity date, and the interest rate will be as per the prevailing rate at the time of extension.

faq.q: Can NRIs invest in the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme?
faq.a: No, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are not eligible to open an SCSS account. The scheme is exclusively for resident Indian senior citizens.
